summary: James G. Mullens is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD at McMaster University and held a post at the University of Saskatchewan in 1989.

James Gibbs (1825–1886) worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. He served as Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai from 1870 to 1879 and as President of the Asiatic Society of Mumbai from circa 1876 to 1881.

James H. Austin (b. 1925) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Nanrei Kobori, Joshu Sasaki, and Katsujo Terayama. He held posts at the Universities of Oregon, Missouri, Colorado, and Idaho, alongside several international sabbatical visiting positions.

James Hadley (1821–1872) was a linguist who studied at Yale College (~1840–1842) and under Edward Elbridge Salisbury (1849). He held posts at Middlebury College (1844–1845) and Yale University (1845–1872).

James Haughton Woods (1864–1935) was an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at Harvard, Strasbourg, and under Paul Deussen, Charles Rockwell Lanman, Arthur Venis, and Mukunda Shastri Adkar, later holding a post at Harvard University in 1914.

James Irving Manatt (1845–1915) worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. Educated at Grinnell and Yale under William Dwight Whitney, he held posts at Denison, Marietta, the University of Nebraska–Lincoln, and served as professor at Brown University (~1892–1915).

James Ishmael Ford (b. 1948) works in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Houn Jiyu-Kennett and John Tarrant, attended the Pacific School of Religion (~1988–1991), and founded Boundless Way Zen (attested 2012).

James Kenneth Powell II is a Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Northwestern University, the University of Chicago, and the University of Wisconsin-Madison (PhD 1998) under teachers including David Tracy, Geshe Lhundub Sopa, Isshi Yamada, and David M. Knipe.
James L. Fitzgerald (b. 1948) is an Indologist who served as a professor at the University of Tennessee (attested 2004–2006) and as Das Professor of Sanskrit at Brown University (attested 2019).

James Mallinson (b. 1970) is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. He earned his D.Phil. at Oxford under Alexis Sanderson (1995–2003) and became Lecturer in Sanskrit and Classical Indian Studies at SOAS University of London in 2013.

James Mark Shields (b. 1971) works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. In 2016, he was attested as an Associate Professor at Bucknell University and an Overseas Collaborative Researcher at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies.
James Matthew Baskind specializes in Japanology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Yale University under the supervision of Stanley Weinstein (attested 2006).

James McHugh is an Indology and religious studies scholar educated at Cambridge, Oxford, and Harvard (PhD), studying under faculty including Lawrence McCrea and Alexis Sanderson. He has held posts at Cornell University and the University of Southern California.

James Miller specializes in Sinology and religious studies. He earned degrees from the University of Cambridge (MA, 1997) and Boston University (PhD, 2000), and was attested in 2014 as Professor at Queen's University Belfast.
James Montgomery (b. 1962) studied at the University of Glasgow (~1980–1989) and joined the Faculty of Asian and Middle Eastern Studies at the University of Cambridge in 1997.
James Morison was an Indologist who studied under Georg Bühler as a Specialschüler and served as a librarian at the University of Oxford (attested 1917–1920).

James Prinsep (1799–1840) worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He was Assistant to the Assay Master at the Kolkata Mint (1819) and a member of the Asiatic Society (1832–1838), where he succeeded Horace Hayman Wilson in 1833.

James R. Ballantyne (1813–1864) was an Indology and philosophy scholar educated at Edinburgh under James Michael and Francis Johnson. He taught at the Scottish Naval and Military Academy, was Principal of Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, and served as India Office librarian.
James Rennell (1742–1830) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served with the East India Company from 1762 to 1777 and joined the Bengal Engineers in 1764.

James Robson (b. 1965) specializes in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He held posts as Assistant Professor at the University of Michigan (attested 2006–2014) and Associate Professor at Harvard University (~2008).
